questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The teaching language (English), the possible courses, and the opportunity to live in a different culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather easy. However, I felt like I received miss leading information about housing prior to my arrival - I was told not to worry about it, however in reality it was quite the challenge to find accomodation at a reasonable price.

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh is very walkable, so distance is not a major issue

Additional comments:

questions.answer: I submitted a prioritized list of 10 courses I would like to attend, and then the courses were allocated - I recieved my top priorities.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote directly to course secretaries who were very helpful.

questions.answer: In general I found the courses to be easier than the ones I take at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar, lectures and course work in smaller groups

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Business Economics (BUST08005)
Fundamentals of Operational Research (MATH10065)
Group Theory (MATH10079)
Principles of Finance (BUST08003)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would reccomend Business Economics and Fundamentals of Operational Research. The professors of both courses are very competent and interesting. Through Business Economics I learned how to use basic economic analyses in practice.

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a wide variety of sports clubs to join (over 50) and at least twice as many societies, where people gather around a common interest.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Hillwalking Club. The people are very nice, and joining their trips is a great way to explore the Scottish Highlands

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get out and see other parts of the country.
